title: Exa 3.0: What's New and What Is Still Unconfirmed
summary: Exa 3.0 is a search quality release affecting automations. Review how this update changes retrieval capabilities for your workflows.
body_markdown:
## Exa released version 3.0 on the date its blog gives


### What Exa is and who makes it


When software needs to find web content and pull it back in a form other software can use, it calls Exa, a search and retrieval service. The Exa Team signs the post, so the maker is Exa itself.


The release bundles retrieval stack improvements with a new search type, **Exa Lite** . The post calls it "the largest improvement to search quality we've ever released." That's the maker's own claim, so treat it as a claim until you've run your own queries.


Two things in that sentence are named but not described by anything I could confirm.


The post names Exa Lite as a new search type, and it names improvements to the retrieval stack, meaning the part of the service that finds and ranks pages before results come back.


I could not confirm the post's wording on what Exa Lite does, how it differs from Exa's existing search types, or which stack changes were made, so I won't paraphrase them here.


The post is dated Oct 19, 2026, which is the release date.


Take the date and the description of Exa Lite straight from the post, and note the day you read them.


### What changes in the request and the response


A search type is something you choose per request.


In Exa's search API it is set by a type field in the request body, next to the query, so a new search type arrives as a new value for a field your step may already send. Exa Lite is announced as one of these.


That much follows from how the post presents it, and the rest I could not confirm.


What I could not confirm is the part that would let you choose between types: what Exa Lite trades away or gains against the types your step calls today, such as speed against depth of ranking.


The same goes for the stack changes.


I found no confirmed new or renamed request fields and no confirmed change to the response shape, which in Exa's API is a list of results, each with fields such as a title and a URL, plus any page contents you asked for.


So the useful reading of the post is narrow. Find the sentence that says what Exa Lite is, the sentence that says how it differs from the existing types, and any mention of a field added, renamed or removed.


Write those down with the date you read them, because they are the specifics the checks and the test later in this article rest on.


### When exa 3.0 was released


If you need the release date, the announcement post itself is dated Oct 19, 2026.


Because the release is new, any third-party tutorial or connector description that predates it describes an older Exa, so check it against the post before you wire anything.


If you build in[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) , check whether the Exa connector exposes Exa Lite before you rely on it.


### How the facts here were checked


I took every fact from Exa's own pages and recorded the day I read them, because a vendor can change a page after you read it.


The set below is what the rest of this article rests on, and a later change to the post would void any line in it.


- Product name: Exa 3.0 ([exa.ai/blog/exa-3](https://exa.ai/blog/exa-3) )
- Maker: Exa, credited as The Exa Team ([exa.ai/blog/exa-3](https://exa.ai/blog/exa-3) )
- Release date: Oct 19, 2026 ([exa.ai/blog/exa-3](https://exa.ai/blog/exa-3) )
- Facts read on: 2026-10-20 ([exa.ai](https://exa.ai/) )


Next come pricing and what each search type does, and they're held to the same standard: only what Exa's pages say, dated to the day they were read.
